label: F-02
title: Cutover loss is borne by stakers (USDe 34.8 bps, 8.93 USDe) while protocol-held value several times larger stays with the protocol: V1 idle buffers left on V1, story-060 surplus relinquished, and the USDe booking haircut accrues as strategy surplus
fingerprintProvenance: Copied verbatim from reports/31/script-audits/stable-staker-v2-cutover/classified-findings.json (not recomputed). finding-manager cross-check: sha256(fingerprintBasis) reproduces it byte-for-byte.
specConformance: standalone (owner-intent memo 2026-08-28; story-082 Background story-060 surplus, Decision 14)
description: Owner migration intent (2026-08-28) says: sweep yield AND the set-aside buffer into principal, relinquish over-credit to the protocol, safe > precise, and 'err toward the USER where possible'. The cutover follows the relinquish leg (story 082 background, story-060 surplus) but none of the user-favouring legs. Frozen V1 excludes its idle buffer from R (known and preserved in V1), and the script leaves those buffers on V1 for a later owner `rescueERC20` (Decision 14). Every migrating staker therefore takes the full exit-plus-re-entry haircut. On USDe the V2 re-deposit books `credit * (1 - 30 bps)` while the swap delivered more, so part of the users' loss immediately becomes strategy surplus attributable to V2 and skimmable by the protocol. Story-060's documented purpose for the DOLA/USDC surplus ('absorbs ... small realized losses in any future terminal migration (R reaches P before users take a haircut)') is also not realized. The memo's intent #2 supersedes that purpose, but story 082 does not say so.
impact: Users lose USDe 8.933848235898477800 (34.805 bps, every holder), USDC 0.170245 (0.865 bps), DOLA 0.004154983888567955 (0.034 bps). Over the same window the protocol keeps 49.845539781409382100 USDe, 10.430694 USDC and 6.997032072106485771 DOLA of idle V1 buffer, plus 26.898455742910213445 DOLA and 27.043385 USDC of relinquished surplus. After migration, V2's `totalBalanceOf - principalOf` shows 4.136480965658327219 USDe, 4.326353 USDC and 2.664877367748603061 DOLA of immediately skimmable surplus. Amounts are small, and the relaxed per-user bounds are disclosed (Decision 4).

classification.assetImpact: About 9 USD of disclosed cutover haircut is borne by stakers (USDe 34.8 bps) while the protocol retains V1 idle buffers, relinquished story-060 surplus and post-migration strategy surplus. This is an opportunity-cost misallocation against the owner-intent memo, not a value leak.
classification.assumptions: Owner-intent memo 2026-08-28 ('err toward the USER where possible') is the operative Law-2 reference.

severityRationale: Capped at QA: the protocol-retained surplus derives from externally-generated yield and buffers, so it is an opportunity cost, never a value leak. The amounts are small and disclosed (Decision 4/14), and owner 'safe > precise' may justify acceptance. It is surfaced as F-type for human disposition, never buried in gas/QA noise. Do not escalate.
recommendation: Either record explicit owner acceptance in story 082 (that users bear the cutover haircut and buffers go to the protocol), or add an optional Phase 7b top-up. `rescueERC20` the V1 idle buffer to OWNER, temporarily `v2.setMigrator(OWNER)`, `depositFor(user, pre - post)` for each migrated user (bounded by the rescued buffer, noting that the USDe top-up is itself haircut 30 bps), then `v2.setMigrator(address(0))`. At minimum, amend story 082 to state where the story-060 surplus goes and why its story-060 purpose no longer applies. Do not introduce a per-client cap as a remedy; the commingled cushion is by design.

dedup.uniquenessVsSiblings: A Law-2 allocation question, measured against the 2026-08-28 owner-intent memo: users bear the haircut while the protocol keeps the buffers and surplus. It is not a verification defect (so distinct from SSV2C-04) and not a slack defect (so distinct from SSV2C-01).
